title: A field relation preserves ordered reciprocity rather than mere adjacency
summary: Specialize the observed ol field relation into a directional two-place relation: when two independently identified fields exchange source and target, the relation should show the predicted inverse or argument-order alternation.

design.mechanism: A recurring field marker encodes an ordered relation between two independently identified argument fields, with a stable inverse behavior under source-target exchange.
design.unit: complete target occurrences with independently established left and right field identities and an adjudicated source-target order
design.contrast: directional reciprocal relation versus symmetric coordination or generic local adjacency
design.prediction: Across held ordered pairs, the marker or its licensed frame should distinguish source-to-target from target-to-source, while a symmetric coordination model predicts no directional change.
design.falsifier: On a predeclared set with independently bound endpoint identities, reversing the endpoint order leaves the same marker and frame without any stable inverse or argument-order effect, while the directional model had required one.
design.scope_note: The source only motivates field relation and does not establish endpoint meanings; this is a conditional design question, not a claim that ol is a relational lexeme.
design.related: Near IDEA000006 reciprocal frame compatibility and the GDT769 R05 field-role dispatch, but changes the unit and falsifier: ordered endpoint reversal rather than mutual frame interchangeability.
design.countermodel: A generic adjacency or coordination marker can appear in nearly symmetric local frames and therefore mimic reciprocity unless endpoint identities and reversal are independently frozen.

source_evidence.quote:
The current atlas contains 376 reader-exact `ol` occurrences. Nine immediate exact amount contacts occur on eight pages and are nearly symmetric around the target. Repeated `ol` field sequences, together with the fact that 58 of 59 apparent line-edge positions remain embedded in continuing records, fit a small relation that travels with a field better than a fixed liquid name. In `f58r.13`, `ol` joins a dry-state field to an independent process field; in `f3r.19`, it joins a cold-dry portion to a dry form. The least committal useful rendering is therefore contextual `und/mit`, with `von/aus` available in an amount attachment.

These local frames justify keeping the relation as the most useful reader default, but they do not produce a role win. R05, R01, and R03 each pass their gates with the same role score of 1.0; R05 is selected only because its dispatch priority is more specific. R01 *Ansatz/Zubereitungsbasis* and R03 measurable product/result are supported rivals, not failed alternatives. Confidence is therefore `C1_LOCAL_FRAME__C0_ROLE_TIEBREAK`. The form is extremely frequent, repetition is not exceptional among frequent forms, and its local environments are broad. Nothing distinguishes plant juice, extract, decoction, medicinal water, oil, wine, or vinegar. Visible similarity between EVA `ol` and Latin *oleum* earns zero identity credit.

design.intake_limit: Raw unreviewed design draft; independent semantic binding is unavailable unless separately established. A positive structural match would not by itself identify an English or German meaning.
design.intake_scope_caution: Ordered relation inversion is not automatically reciprocity. A directional relation may keep the same written marker while argument order supplies direction. Before testing, freeze the endpoint-role interpretation and a predicted difference that is not already the observed swap; invariant marker shape alone is not a falsifier.
